nodes.title: Fraction Parts
nodes.objective: Identify a fraction as equal parts of a whole.
nodes.concept: A fraction names part of a whole.
nodes.explanation: The numerator tells how many equal parts we have. The denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole.

visual.text: Tap segments to explore parts. In 2/6: 2 is the numerator (parts shaded) and 6 is the denominator (total equal parts).

nodes.title: Equivalent Fractions
nodes.objective: Recognize two fractions that represent the same quantity.
nodes.concept: Equivalent fractions name the same amount.
nodes.explanation: For example, 1/2 and 2/4 represent the exact same part of a whole.

visual.text: Shade 2 out of 4 parts (2/4). Notice that 2/4 covers the exact same area as 1/2 of the whole strip.

nodes.title: Adding Fractions
nodes.objective: Add fractions with the same denominator.
nodes.concept: Keep the denominator and add the numerators.
nodes.explanation: For same denominators: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5. The denominator stays 5 because the slice size does not change.

visual.text: Combine 1 fifth and 2 fifths: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5. Tap to see 3 fifths shaded.

questions.prompt: What does the denominator tell us?

options.text: How many parts we have selected
options.feedback: Remember: The TOP number (numerator) tells how many parts we have selected.

options.text: How many equal parts make the whole
options.feedback: Correct! The denominator names the total equal divisions that make up the whole.

options.text: The total score of the lesson
options.feedback: Denominator is a mathematical term for the bottom number of a fraction.
The denominator counts ALL equal parts together (shaded plus unshaded).

questions.prompt: If a paper strip is divided into 8 equal parts and 3 parts are colored blue, what fraction is colored?

options.feedback: 3/5 compares colored parts to uncolored parts. A fraction must compare colored parts to the WHOLE (8).
Correct! 3 colored parts over 8 total equal parts gives 3/8.
Remember: The colored count goes on TOP (numerator) and total parts on the BOTTOM (denominator).
5/8 is the uncolored part. Re-read the question carefully to find the fraction that is colored.

questions.prompt: Why does cutting a shape into 4 pieces NOT always make fourths (1/4)?

options.text: Because fractions only work with 2 pieces
options.feedback: Fractions can be divided into any number of parts, not just 2.

options.text: Because the 4 pieces must be strictly EQUAL in size
options.feedback: Exactly! In fractions, every part must be identical in size to represent 1/4.
Even or odd numbers can both make fractions if the parts are equal.
In a proper fraction, the top number is naturally smaller than the bottom.

questions.prompt: Which fraction represents the same quantity as 1/2?

options.feedback: 1/3 is smaller than 1/2 because splitting a whole into 3 pieces makes each piece smaller.
Correct! 2 out of 4 parts covers the exact same area as 1 out of 2 parts.
Half of 5 is 2.5, so 3/5 is more than half.
2/5 is less than half.

questions.prompt: If you take 1/3 of a chocolate bar and split every piece in half, what fraction do you have?

options.feedback: When you split every piece in half, the total number of pieces doubles too!
Correct! 1 piece becomes 2, and 3 total pieces become 6: 1/3 = 2/6.
1/6 is the size of a single smaller piece. Consider how many of those smaller pieces you hold.
Doubling 3 pieces gives 6 pieces, not 5.

questions.prompt: Which fraction is 4/8 in its simplest equivalent form?

options.feedback: Divide numerator and denominator by 4; do not subtract.
Correct! 4 is half of 8, so 4/8 simplifies directly to 1/2.
Dividing both numerator and denominator by 4 gives the simplest equivalent form.
4/4 is one whole. 4/8 is one half.
Denominators indicate the size of equal slices. When adding like fractions, the slice size does not change.
Remember to add both numerators: 1 + 2 = 3.
Correct! When denominators are equal, keep the denominator and add numerators: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5.
Combine both quantities together: 1 + 2 = 3 fifths.

questions.prompt: A roti is divided into 8 equal parts. Simran eats 2/8 and Aman eats 3/8. How much did they eat in total?

options.feedback: The total equal divisions of the roti remain unchanged. Combine the portions eaten without altering the total divisions.
Correct! 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8 of the roti.
Carefully recount the combined parts eaten by both persons.
They ate the pieces together, so add the amounts.

questions.prompt: When adding like fractions (such as 2/7 + 3/7), why does the denominator stay 7?

options.text: Because the size of each equal part (sevenths) has not changed
options.feedback: Brilliant! The denominator names the size of the piece (sevenths). Adding pieces changes only the count, not the piece size.

options.text: Because denominators can never be changed in mathematics
options.feedback: Denominators change when finding common denominators or multiplying.

options.text: Because the numerator is more important than denominator
options.feedback: Both numerator and denominator are equally essential in defining a fraction.

options.text: Because addition only works on odd numbers
options.feedback: Addition operates identically on all numbers.
